docs.title: Rivet
docs.text:
Rivet is a small framework written in Typescript that allows for easy server creation. Rivet is very lightweight and idles at 2mb of memory, for comparision Express idles at over 50mb or more!

Rivet can be used in a lot of aplications, since it is very easy to implement and has a very simular API to Express!

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Rivet is pretty feature-filled, here are the all the features:

  1. Static file serving
  2. Custom error handlers
  3. Route handlers
  4. Body parsing
  5. Parameters
  6. Plugin support
  7. WebSocket(via plugin)
  8. CORS

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Rivet is incredibly simple, for example this is all the code needed to run a basic server! 

import { Rivet, RivetResponse } from '@igosprojects/rivet'
import { IncomingMessage } from 'http'

const app = new Rivet();

app.get('/', (req: IncomingMessage, res: RivetResponse) => {
        res.send("Hello, Rivet!");
});

app.start(8080);

docs.title: Api list
docs.text:
• app.branch(prefix, subApp)
  • app.cors(options)
  • app.error(code, handler)
  • app.get(path, handler)
  • app.OnServerCreate(callback)
  • app.post(path, handler)
  • app.RateLimit(options)
  • app.start(port, host?, callback?)
  • app.static(prefix, directory)
  • app.use(plugin)
  • app.UseMiddleware(middleware)
  • app.SendError(code, req, res)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Arguments in Rivet are used to for example read URL args passed on. Arguments are passed in the URL and can be read at runtime using req.params.

docs.title: USAGE
docs.text:
The following code will log the "id" argument to the console:

app.get("/", (req: IncommingMessage, res: RivetResponse) => {
    console.log(`id: ${req.params.id}`);
    res.send("logged!");
})

docs.title: Body parsing
docs.text: Rivet offers body parsing, body parsing allows to get data sent by forms, external tools and the browser.

docs.title: USAGE
docs.text:
To use body parsing you simply need to read the req.body property. Please note! The property may be a string an object or an key value object, it is recommended to check for the correct type!!

Here is a small example, this code will return the passed in body to the client(please note that this is not fully safe!)

// Get requests dont have a body
app.post("/", (req: IncommingMessage, res: RivetResponse) => {
    res.json(req.body); // Send back the sent body
})

docs.title: Branching
docs.text: Branching in Rivet works by using the app.branch function. The function allows for you to "branch" another Rivet app to the current one. When the any requests to prefix/* are made, they will be passed down to the app attached

docs.title: ARGUMENTS
docs.text: The first argument to app.branch is the prefix, for example "/api". The second argument is the app to attach to the current app, for example "APIApp"

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: Rivet allows for custom error handlers to be defined like the app.getfunction.

docs.title: USAGE
docs.text:
To define a new error handler you can use the app.error function, for example this code will when a 404 error happens respond with "url not found on the server!"

app.error(404, (err, req: IncommingMessage, res: RivetResponse) => {
    res.send("url not found on the server!");
});

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
In normal HTML forms you can use the req.body variable, since they are passed on the HTTP body instead of a special field. For example this code will print the passed in name to the console(the usage is the same but "req.fields" is changed to "req.body") 

app.post("/", (req: IncommingMessage, res: RivetResponse) => {
    const { name } = req.body; // Get the name field
    console.log(name);
})

docs.title: Files
docs.text: File uploads in Rivet are pretty simple, all the files uploaded on that request are put into req.files. To get a specific file you can use the req.file() method with the file name passed in.

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
Unlike non multipart forms to get the text in a form using Rivet you can use the req.fields variable. For example, this code will print the uploaded name to the console: 

app.post("/", (req: IncommingMessage, res: RivetResponse) => {
    const { name } = req.fields; // Get the name field
    console.log(name);
})

docs.title: Static files
docs.text: Static files in Rivet can be served using the app.static method, the method accepts a prefix and a directory path. For example running this will serve the files from "/public" to "/" app.static("/public", "/");

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text: Middleware in Rivet is the (kinda)same as plugins, but instead of running once it runs every request!

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text:
Here is the middleware type from src/types.ts: 

export type Middleware = (req: IncomingMessage, res: RivetResponse, next: () =>

Its very small cause middleware is actually just a function! It recives the request and the response and it can modify them or handle the request based on what the creator made it do.

docs.title: Javascript Example
docs.text:
Here is a small example of a middleware that prints Recived Request! when a request happens: 

function MyMiddleware(req, res, next)  {
    console.log("Recived request!");
    next();
}

docs.title: Typescript Example
docs.text:
Here is a small example of a middleware that prints Recived Request! when a request happens, but in Typescript: 

function MyMiddleware(req: IncomingMessage, res: RivetResponse, next: () => void)  {
    console.log("Recived request!");
    next();
}

docs.title: How do i install middleware?
docs.text: To install middleware in Rivet you can use the app.UseMiddleware function

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text: Plugins in Rivet are incredibly simple, infact they are just a Javascript object with an install function. Here is a short explanation of them, and how they work.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text:
Plugins are very simple, here is their entire type definition. Its very small and pretty much all you need to have is install! 

export interface RivetPlugin {
    name: string;
    version?: string;
    install(app: Rivet): void | Promise<void>;
};
Now lets go thru them, plugins can but dont have to include a version, the name is required tho! The install function can be a Promise function or a normal function, the install function is called when app.use is passed the plugin.

docs.title: PLEASE NOTE
docs.text: Plugins run only once on startup, they ussualy register middleware and run one time init!

docs.title: Javascript Example
docs.text:
Here is a very minimal plugin that prints Loaded Plugin! on loading(JS version): 

const myPlugin = {
    name: 'my-plugin',
    install(app) {
        console.log('Loaded Plugin!');
    }
};

docs.title: Typescript Example
docs.text:
Here is the same minimal plugin but for usage with Typescript(make sure to add the imports!): 

import { RivetPlugin } from '@igosprojects/rivet'

const myPlugin: RivetPlugin = {
    name: 'my-plugin',
    install(app: Rivet): void {
        console.log('Loaded Plugin!');
    }
};

docs.title: Coding
docs.text: Rivet has a simple API that is suprisingly easy to use! If you havent allready read the setup part first!

docs.title: NOTICE
docs.text: All the examples will use Typescript as its my comfort language and the one used to make Rivet!

docs.title: IMPORTING
docs.text:
To initilize Rivet you first need to import it, that can be done using the import statement in ES modules(Typescript is by defualt ES!) So this code will import Rivet and let you use its types: 

import { Rivet } from '@igosprojects/rivet'
Now you have imported Rivet, remember this we will edit it a bit later on! Proceed to the next section

docs.title: CREATING THE APP OBJECT
docs.text:
To create the app object we need to make a new Rivet object. To do that add the following code to your file: 

const app = new Rivet();

docs.title: Creating routes
docs.text:
To create new routes using Rivet you can use the app.get function. It lets you assign handlers to GET routes. For example this code will send back "Hello, Rivet!" when the route "/" is accessed: 

app.get('/', (req: IncomingMessage, res: RivetResponse) => {
    res.send("Hello, Rivet!");
});
NOTE: The below section is for if you are using Typescript

Notice the new types? IncomingMessage and RivetResponse are not defined yet! If you try to compile it will fail like so: To fix that, replace your Rivet import with: 

import { Rivet, RivetResponse } from '@igosprojects/rivet'
And add this import for IncomingMessage 
import { IncomingMessage } from 'http'

Now the compile errors should be fixed!

docs.title: Starting the server
docs.text:
Now to start the server, we will use the app.start function for this, so you can add this to you code: 

app.start(8080);
That will start the Rivet server on localhost port 8080. If you want to you can configure a custom IP or open on all interfaces. You can use the second argument, so doing this will open on all interfaces: 
app.start(8080, '0.0.0.0');

docs.title: Final result
docs.text:
The final result should look something like this: 

import { Rivet, RivetResponse } from '@igosprojects/rivet'
import { IncomingMessage } from 'http'

const app = new Rivet();

app.get('/', (req: IncomingMessage, res: RivetResponse) => {
        res.send("Hello, Rivet!");
});

app.start(8080);

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
To run your newly created Rivet app you will need to run it using Node, if you are on Typescript read #typescript. So running on raw Node is easy you just need to do: 

node PATH_TO_FILE
So if your file is index.js you can do: 
node index.js

docs.title: Typescript
docs.text:
On Typescript you will first need to compile, so you can run: 

npx tsc
That should produce source files depending on where you configured the outDirsetting, for me its in the same folder as the source so i can run: 
node index.js

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: To start developing on Rivet you will need some basic setup. Rivet is based on NodeJS so if you havent installed it go on and do that! Once NodeJS is installed go read #installing(unless you havent setup an NPM project yet)

docs.title: Setting up an NPM project
docs.text:
To setup an NPM project you will need to first have NPM, it comes with NodeJS so that will allready be done! Anyway, lets initilize the project. To initilize an NPM project we use: 

npm init -y
If you want to manually input the info(name, author, license, description), remove the -y.

Now it has created a package.json file, now you can move onto installing Rivet

docs.title: Installing
docs.text:
To install Rivet you need to use NPM. So you can run this command: 

npm install @igosprojects/rivet
BOOM! Thats it, its not complicated unless you are a Typescript user, it needs more setup that we talk about #typescript. Now move onto the next section where we setup the basic code.

docs.title: Typescript
docs.text:
Typescript needs some more setup to get up and running, for that add the @types/node package: 

npm install -D @types/node
(-D specifies dev package, it wont be included if you package it or make it an NPM package)

And if you have a Typescript project setup add node to your types config. Here is a sample tsconfig.json: 

{
  // Visit https://aka.ms/tsconfig to read more about this file
  "compilerOptions": {
    // File Layout
    // "rootDir": "./src",
    // "outDir": "./dist",

    // Environment Settings
    // See also https://aka.ms/tsconfig/module
    "module": "nodenext",
    "target": "esnext",
    // For nodejs:
    // "lib": ["esnext"],
    "types": ["node"],
    // and npm install -D @types/node

    // Other Outputs
    "sourceMap": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "declarationMap": true,

    // Stricter Typechecking Options
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,
    "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true,

    // Style Options
    // "noImplicitReturns": true,
    // "noImplicitOverride": true,
    // "noUnusedLocals": true,
    // "noUnusedParameters": true,
    // "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true,
    // "noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature": true,

    // Recommended Options
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "noUncheckedSideEffectImports": true,
    "moduleDetection": "force",
    "skipLibCheck": true,
  }
}
